children.subject: An Admin order timestamp and the REST createdDate are the same instant; Admin prints no offset while the API returns UTC with Z
children.question: Why does the order time on the Admin screen differ by hours from the createdDate in the REST payload?
children.body: They are the same instant in two timezones. Admin prints an order timestamp with no offset; the API returns UTC with an explicit Z. So comparing a timestamp off a screenshot with one off a payload, without converting, shows a discrepancy of however many hours the reader happens to be from UTC, and it is not a discrepancy. This bites hardest when a screenshot is the evidence in a bug report and the reader is in a different timezone from the person who took it.

children.subject: Admin order timestamps were attributed to the viewer's browser timezone, and a later observation traces them to the operator's profile timezone
children.question: Does Admin render an order timestamp in the browser's local timezone or in some other timezone?
children.body:
Round one's arm C read Sep 15, 2026 5:51:39 AM on the Admin order screen for the instant the REST payload reports as 2026-09-15T09:51:39.6897076Z - a four-hour offset, that session's browser being at UTC-4. Admin renders in the viewer's local time.

**Disputed.** The offset is not the browser's. Admin renders order timestamps in the timezone stored on the operator's PLATFORM PROFILE: GET /api/platform/profiles/currentuser returns VirtoCommerce.Platform.UI.TimeZone=America/New_York, and the order blade printed Sep 15 2026 4:17:18 AM for a createdDate of 2026-09-15T08:17:18.308Z and Sep 10 2026 3:51:56 PM for 2026-09-10T19:51:56Z - both UTC-4 - while this machine's browser is Asia/Yerevan, UTC+4 (would have been 12:17 PM and 11:51 PM). Proof the browser is not the source: a cold deep link to the same blade, which loads before the profile does, printed the same instant as 2026-09-15 PM12:17:18 in the browser's zone and a ja-JP format. So two operators see different clock times on one order according to a per-user setting, and the same blade also prints its indexation widget in raw UTC (Indexed Sep 15 2026 8:21:52 am against modifiedDate 08:21:51Z).

why: (a) two different APIs a reader reaches separately: the seoinfos search behaviour and an unrelated side finding on the duplicates endpoint

children.subject: POST /api/seoinfos/search needs storeId and matches a permalink path, never the bare slug field
children.question: How do I check with POST /api/seoinfos/search whether a semantic URL is already taken?
children.body: POST /api/seoinfos/search without storeId returns 500 'Store with ID not found'. With storeId and languageCode, the slug field returned no matches even for slugs known to exist; the permalink field works, but it is resolved as a path under the store's SEO link type. With Long links, a category under a top-level category matches only as parent-slug/child-slug, and a product only by its full path. The bare slug of a nested object returns nothing. A freshly written product SEO record is found immediately through its full path, so the search reads the database, not the index.

why: (a) two different APIs a reader reaches separately: the isActive switch and its effect on the storefront product, versus a counting trap in the configurations search endpoint

children.subject: ProductConfiguration.isActive flips Product.isConfigurable on the next storefront query with no reindex
children.question: How do I turn a product's configurability off, and how soon does the storefront see it?
children.body: isActive on the ProductConfiguration is the switch, it is honoured immediately, and NO REINDEX is involved. Saving the configuration with isActive false through POST /api/catalog/products/configurations flipped the storefront's Product.isConfigurable from true to false on the very next query, and turning it on had flipped it to true the same way seconds after the configuration was first created -- so isConfigurable is computed from the configuration entity at resolve time, not baked into the search index document, and waiting for or triggering a reindex to make a configurability change visible is wasted work. The product's own index entry is untouched by any of this: price, buyability and stock are unchanged, and the Admin product blade's index timestamp does not move.

children.subject: An empty-criteria configurations search counts deactivated configurations, not configurable products
children.question: Does POST /api/catalog/products/configurations/search with an empty body count only products a buyer can configure?
children.body: POST /api/catalog/products/configurations/search with an EMPTY criteria body counts configurations, not CONFIGURABLE PRODUCTS -- it includes deactivated ones. Measured on one product: empty body totalCount 1, {isActive:true} totalCount 0, {isActive:false} totalCount 1, with the product reading isConfigurable false. Since nothing can delete a configuration, a deactivated row is the permanent end state of every configuration anyone ever experiments with, so this gap widens over a store's life and never closes. Ask with {isActive:true} when the question is how many products a buyer can actually configure.
